validated_results.title: Legume and isoflavone intake and prostate cancer risk: The Multiethnic Cohort Study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study investigating dietary soy product intake and incident prostate cancer risk in the Multiethnic Cohort.

extraction.population: Multiethnic Cohort Study (African Americans, Native Hawaiians, Japanese Americans, Latinos, and Whites)

sample_size.excerpt: The analyses included 82,483 men who completed a detailed quantitative food frequency questionnaire in 1993–1996. A total of 4,404 prostate cancer cases including 1,278 nonlocalized or high-grade cases were recorded during the average follow-up period of 8 years.
sample_size.location: Material and methods, Study cohort, paragraph 1

cases.location: Material and methods, Case ascertainment, paragraph 1

effect_size.excerpt: Among men with the highest intake of legumes, the risk reduction was 11% for total prostate cancer (RR = 0.89, 95% CI = 0.80–0.99, p for trend = 0.007) and 26% for nonlocalized or high-grade cancer (RR = 0.74, 95% CI = 0.61–0.90, p for trend = 0.007) compared to men with the lowest intake.

design.excerpt: The design and implementation of the Multiethnic Cohort Study (MEC) has been described in detail previously.
design.location: Material and methods, Study cohort, paragraph 1

timing.excerpt: A total of 4,404 prostate cancer cases were recorded during the average follow-up period of 8 years.
timing.location: Material and methods, Case ascertainment, paragraph 1

continent.excerpt: Participants are mainly from 5 racial/ethnic populations in Hawaii and Los Angeles, California
continent.location: Material and methods, Study cohort, paragraph 1

ethnicity.excerpt: the Multiethnic Cohort Study in Hawaii and Los Angeles

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Dietary intake at baseline was assessed by a self-administered quantitative food frequency questionnaire (QFFQ).
exposure_measurement.location: Material and methods, Dietary assessment, paragraph 1
